title: Tyler Smith returns from injury: What it means for Cowboys offense against Buccaneers - CBS Sports
description: The Cowboys survived without Smith, but his return gives Dallas a boost against Tampa
body:
The Cowboys survived without Smith, but his return gives Dallas a boost against Tampa

    10:38 am ET

            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        ARLINGTON, Texas -- Three-time Pro Bowl left guard Tyler Smith is back with the Dallas Cowboys, just in time for "Thursday Night Football" against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Smith practiced as a limited participant in Monday's walkthrough and in Tuesday's practice before being a full participant in Wednesday's walkthrough. He is on track to be active tonight against Tampa, per a team source. "You just get a guy like that back, an enforcer, one of the best guards, if not the best guard in the league. It definitely helps," Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott said after practice on Tuesday. Smith had yet to suit up this season after undergoing thumb surgery days before their season opener and some time on injured reserve."It was extremely difficult," Smith said after practice on Monday. "It was one of the hardest things I've gone through. ... "I couldn't grab, I couldn't punch. … I just couldn't do my job as an o-lineman. We hand fight. We see somebody every play. It's not like I'm in space or I'm dropping back or I'm tackling somebody. I have to block, and I have to manhandle somebody every play. So that was my biggest issue. If I could do all those things with no issues, then we don't have a problem."   
The Cowboys gave Smith the ultimate decision on whether he wanted to wait another week after his practice window opened, but he gave the team the green light to line him up on Thursday night. "If Tyler feels good that he can go play, then I have no problem," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "I've seen him, like I said, play football at a very high level. It's more of a comfort level for him than me. All Tyler's got to do is say, 'Hey Schotty, I feel good' and he'll be out there.'"     Smith's impactSo what will materially change for a Cowboys offense that is already averaging the most points per drive (3.39) in the NFL, a figure that actually ranks as the fourth-most by any team through their first four games of a season in the 21st century, per CBS Sports Research? 
The versatility in Dallas' run game, which ranks as the eighth-worst in the league, with an average of 89.5 rushing yards per game. Teams that face the Cowboys know they don't feel incredibly confident running the football to the left with undrafted veteran T.J. Bass at left guard. The Cowboys have run to the right side of the line at the ninth-highest rate in the NFL this season (35.9%) and to the left side of the line at the fourth-lowest rate (26.9%) without Smith this season. They're around league average in run-up-the-middle rate, at 20th (44.7%). Now that Smith is back, his return unlocks the ability to run the football to any and all locations along the line of scrimmage.

title: Aaron Judge pushes for Yankees to go 'all-in' this offseason after disappointing playoff exit - CBS Sports
description: Judge missed the postseason with a calf injury and is now looking ahead to 2027
body:
Judge missed the postseason with a calf injury and is now looking ahead to 2027
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 8, 2026

    9:48 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For the third time in their last three postseason trips, the New York Yankees were eliminated at home Wednesday night. The Yankees dropped Game 3 to the AL East rival Tampa Bay Rays and were swept in the best-of-five ALDS. New York again piled up wins during the regular season, then wilted against equal or better competition in the postseason. Perhaps the outcome would have been different if reigning two-time AL MVP Aaron Judge had been able to play, or perhaps not. Judge was relegated to spectator during the postseason due a lingering September calf injury. Following the Game 3 loss, Judge implored the team's brain trust to go all-in this offseason, and improve the roster however they can. "We're the Yankees. I feel like they should go all-in and do what they need to do," Judge said. "And if we got holes, it's finding certain players or personnel, whatever we need, we got to go out there and get it. That's why I signed back here to play with the Yankees, is to fight for a championship every single year and go all-in. That's what I do every offseason is to get ready to give this team and this city everything I got. So I expect them to do the same." 
This is a bad offseason to go all-in. The free agent class is very week behind reigning two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, and the Yankees are one of the few teams that can plausibly say it doesn't make sense to prioritize Skubal. On paper, their rotation runs six deep with Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Carlos Rodón, Cam Schlittler, Will Warren, and Ryan Weathers. 
Also, it is a near certainly the owners will lock out the players when the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. At that point, the hot stove will freeze, and no transactions will be allowed. And, once the lockout ends, there will be a truncated spring training that won't leave much time for roster moves. It will be a disjointed offseason, for sure. The Yankees go into the offseason needing upgrades at second base, third base, center field, and in the bullpen. They can fill some of those positions internally (Anthony Volpe at second, Spencer Jones in center, etc.), but, as Judge said, these are the Yankees, and they should strive for something better than good enough. 
New York went 93-68 and had the AL's second-best record during the regular season. Their current 17-year World Series drought is tied for the franchise's longest with 1979-95.

        Missouri freshman offensive lineman DJ Jones is recovering after receiving a heart transplant, coach Eli Drinkwitz announced Thursday. I have a great update to share on DJ," Drinkwitz wrote on social media. "Last night, DJ received his heart transplant, and his surgery went well. He is now recovering. We are incredibly grateful for the medical team who cared for DJ and for the donor and donor family whose extraordinary gift made this possible."Please continue to keep DJ, his family, the donor family, and his caregivers in your prayers as he begins the recovery process.We are so thankful for the incredible prayers and support from the entire Mizzou Family. We will continue to update you when wecan."During normal freshman intake, Missouri's health staff did a full evaluation of Jones and flagged a heart problem. When it didn't improve over the course of two weeks, Jones was sent to the Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville, Florida, where a "much more significant issue" was discovered. 
Rated the No. 108 overall player by 247Sports, Jones was rated the top overall recruit in Missouri's star-studded 2026 recruiting class. A native of Venice, Florida, Jones was projected as a future NFL Draft pick after picking Missouri over a laundry list of elite offers. Unfortunately, he remains away from the team in Jacksonville during the Tigers' blazing start to the season. No. 14 Missouri defeated previously unbeaten Florida 45-17 last week, Drinkwitz's best win with the Tigers. "It's just hard, an 18-year-old with everything in front of him, and you're just never prepared for that kind of news," Drinkwitz said. "Our team was not prepared for that news. We're praying for him, and we hope that Mizzou fans are joining in with us because he needs help in a hurry. We're pulling for you, buddy."
Jones has not appeared in a game this season.

body:
Kenneth Walker III's league-leading ground game and Steve Spagnuolo's revamped, pressure-heavy defense are taking the burden off Patrick Mahomes
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:02 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Kansas City Chiefs had won the AFC West nine consecutive years before missing the playoffs last season. For the majority of the decade, they were a free space on the NFL's postseason Bingo card. But in 2025, for the first time in Patrick Mahomes' career, the media stopped giving the franchise the benefit of the doubt regarding being one of the last teams standing. After four weeks of this year's regular season, Kansas City looks like the formidable Kansas City teams of old. While legacy names such as tight end Travis Kelce and defensive tackle Chris Jones are still around, several newcomers, including a strong rookie defensive class, have inspired newfound confidence — and taken the burden off Mahomes to get the Chiefs back to Super Bowl contention.Prized free agent running back acquisition Kenneth Walker III leads the NFL in rushing (537) yards as the league trends more run heavy, but it was a defensive overhaul that has been the biggest change for the Chiefs. Roughly 35% of defensive snaps this season have been played by those who were not on the roster a year ago.How Chiefs' defense has improvedIn terms of defensive EPA per play, through four weeks, the Chiefs have their best mark (0.04) since winning the Super Bowl in 2024. The pass rush is a big reason for that improvement. 
Kansas City is on pace for 259 pressures, according to TruMedia, which would be the team's highest total in a decade. Last season, it generated a higher team pressure rate (39.2%), but that effort required more blitzes. Steve Spagnuolo's defense is impacting the opposing quarterback without sending five-plus rushers as often, which takes some pressure off an entirely revamped secondary. The problem thus far has been finishing plays. Despite the uptick in pressure, Kansas City has just four sacks on the year, tied for the second-lowest in the NFL.      The reason for elevated success up front has been improved play from stalwarts Felix Anudike-Uzomah and George Karlaftis, as well as working rookies R Mason Thomas and Peter Woods — both of whom were taken top-40 overall — into the rotation. The former is third on the team with 10 pressures. Upon trading Trent McDuffie and allowing cornerback Jaylen Watson and safety Bryan Cook to depart in free agency, the franchise countered by drafting LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane No. 6 overall. It also signed veteran safety Alohi Gilman and brought back cornerback L'Jarius Sneed, whom they had traded to the Titans in 2024. Second-year cornerback Nohl Williams is more than halfway to last season's total snaps played. 
Although inexperienced at this level, Williams and Delane have shown enough to suggest they could be even better than some of the duos Kansas City has employed in recent years. Spagnuolo requires his defensive backs to play the run and tackle. Delane has shown a willingness to play downhill,but has room for improvement in coming to balance in space and finishing tackles. The team saved money by moving McDuffie and not signing the aforementioned veterans from last year's team. The savings were funneled toward the addition of Walker and others — a redistribution of resources. Opposing quarterbacks have the fourth-lowest passer rating against the Chiefs this season. The re-made secondary is doing its job. Walker III has taken the load off MahomesThe Chiefs' pass attack is still not where it needs to be, especially given injuries, but establishing the run game has made the franchise less one-dimensional. They have more answers than simply requiring Mahomes to be Superman. An injury to Tyquan Thornton may lead the organization to pursue its options, which are expanded to include former Chief Tyreek Hill and the Browns' Jerry Jeudy. 
Aside from Kelce, the team's primary outlets in the pass game are Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy. Jalen Royal's three receptions are the only other contributions from the receiver room. The offensive line has also not gone according to plan, but I have already written extensively about the unit, particularly undrafted free-agent left tackle Kahlil Benson. The early-season schedule has not been overly stimulating, but the path ahead is not littered with obstacles either. Enjoying a bye this week and embracing an early-season chance to get healthy, the team returns to action next week against the floundering Chargers. As one of three undefeated teams, the Chiefs are well on the way to a postseason return.

title: The Six Pack: Picks for Oregon-UCLA, Alabama-Georgia and lock of Week 6 - CBS Sports
description: The parity in college football seems to exist in tiers. A few weeks ago, in this column, I shared data showing that underdogs were winni
body:
The parity in college football seems to exist in tiers. A few weeks ago, in this column, I shared data showing that underdogs were winning games at a lower rate than at any time in recent history. That same separation exists between teams ranked in the AP Top 25 and those who aren't.It's fun to call anyone who votes in the poll an idiot and tell them what they got wrong, but overall, they seem to know what they're talking about. Ranked teams are 85-6 against unranked teams so far this season. That .934 win percentage is easily the highest rate in the College Football Playoff Era. The next-highest was 0.852 in 2014. And it extends further than straight-up winning. Ranked teams have gone 47-43-1 against the spread against unranked teams, too. That's a .522 win percentage, which may not seem very high, but it's the highest since the 2019 season, when they finished with a cover rate of .547. Only three other seasons saw ranked teams finish over .500 ATS (2021, 2022, 2023), and none of those seasons was higher than .514.
Obviously, there's a lot of season left to go, and things could even out, but it is interesting that all five of the 12 seasons in which ranked teams finished (or are currently) above .500 ATS have come in the last seven seasons. We may be seeing more parity at the top of the sport among title contenders, but there's evidence that the gap between the elite and the next tier is widening.Games of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 21 UCLA at No. 13 OregonUCLA has been one of the bigger surprises to start the season. Many people pegged the Bruins as a potential sleeper before the year began due to Bob Chesney taking over the program and an infusion of talent and investment. Plus, the schedule wasn't overly taxing compared to what others in the Big Ten might face. So far, the Bruins have lived up to their potential.They get their biggest test of the year this weekend, though. A road trip against Oregon -- even an Oregon that's been underperforming -- is never easy, and the Ducks pose a far bigger challenge than any of UCLA's first four opponents. 
My concern for UCLA here is that, as successful as they've been, they're a bit one-dimensional on offense. Now, if you're going to be one-dimensional, be great at that dimension. UCLA has been so far. This is the best rushing attack in the country from a success-rate and EPA-rate perspective. It's also one of the most explosive rushing attacks going. The problem UCLA faces is that it hasn't found itself in a position where it has to drop back and pass, which is beneficial because its passing offense hasn't been nearly as sharp.Oregon's defensive line is the best they've seen by far and could limit what the Bruins do on the ground, putting them in more adverse situations. At the same time, Oregon has questions of its own. Dante Moore is back at practice. We do not yet know his status for this game, as he recovers from a concussion sustained against USC. Signs point to a possible return, but Dylan Raiola was outstanding in relief. We don't know which direction Dan Lanning will go, and those questions lead to some skepticism about what the Ducks' offense will look like. So when I add up questions about how effectively UCLA will run the ball against Oregon, with questions about who will be at QB for the Ducks, it leads me in one direction. The Pick: Under 58.5 (-114) at Fanduel

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 Georgia at No. 6 AlabamaThe biggest question about this game is the weather. As I write this, Tropical Storm Isaias is heading toward the Gulf Coast and is expected to intensify into a hurricane. The forecast calls for heavy rainfall and gusty winds in central Alabama from Friday into Saturday. That's why the total for this game has plummeted from an opening number of 56.5 to 52.5.That's a lot, but it's not enough to scare me away from the pick.I have questions about both teams. Alabama is certainly more tested than Georgia to this point, but it hasn't gone up against a front seven like Georgia's. Nor has Georgia faced many offenses that can test its defense, particularly an offense with a quarterback like Keelon Russell. Also, we saw Georgia's offense struggle against Oklahoma. They scored 41 points thanks to defensive scores and short fields created by turnovers, but on a per-play basis, it was Georgia's worst performance of the season by far. That's not unexpected against Oklahoma, but while this Alabama defense isn't to the level of the Sooners, it's proven to be pretty good. So the unanswered questions for both offenses, combined with the weather that won't help either offense, make this one an easy call. Frankly, I won't be shocked if this number continues to plummet as we get closer to kick. The Pick: Under 52.5 (-110) at DraftKings
Lock of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 10 LSU at KentuckyThis will surprise many of you, but contrary to popular belief, I don't like to be the "well, actually" guy. I want Kentucky fans to just be able to enjoy the fact that they've already secured two unexpected road wins this year and are 4-1 despite entering the season with a projected win total of 4.5. And they should be happy! Winning is fun, and it's even better when nobody expected it from you.But I'm not buying in. Not completely. Kentucky may be better than expected, but Texas A&M and South Carolina are much worse than expected, too. Now the Wildcats are back at home to face an LSU team that's banged up but has a pretty clear talent advantage. The line has moved in Kentucky's favor this week, but it's reached a point where I see far too much value on the Tigers to pass it up. Perhaps Kentucky will prove me wrong yet again, or perhaps the market has overreacted a bit to their success and LSU injuries. I know which side I'm leaning toward. The Pick: LSU -8.5 (-112) at DraftKingsRed River Rock Fight of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 1 Texas vs. OklahomaHere's a fun fact for you (unless you're an Oklahoma fan): Oklahoma has not scored a touchdown against Texas since both schools were still in the Big 12. That's right, the Longhorns have held the Sooners to three field goals each of the last two seasons in 34-3 and 23-6 victories. That's one of the reasons why we see a total this low.
It's wild to think about, considering the history between these two, and how many times this meeting has been a high-scoring shootout, but things have changed. Oklahoma's defense remains elite, but the offense is stuck deep in the mud. John Mateer has been bad and has not been helped by his offensive line. Oklahoma can't run the ball, can't pass the ball, and can't hold onto the ball, either. It's a poor recipe for success.But it's not as if the Texas offense has been great itself. While they're better than Oklahoma's unit, the Longhorns' offense ranks outside the top 40 in points per drive, EPA per play, and success rate. Their explosive play rate of 10.8% ranks 104th nationally. Their saving grace has been improved play in the red zone, where their 4.74 points per trip ranks only 42nd nationally but is an improvement over recent seasons. Now, in Texas' defense, it's played a tough schedule so far this year. But while that's true, it's not like Oklahoma's defense presents an easier challenge than what the Longhorns have faced. The Pick: Under 39.5 (-110) at FanduelAnother Under of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    San Diego State at Oregon StateListen, I didn't come into the week saying "I can't wait to pick four unders and root against touchdowns all weekend," but it appears that's what I'll be doing. This pick is a little scary considering how good Oregon State's offense has been to start the season.
Seriously, if you aren't familiar with the 2026 Beavers, you should pay attention. They're a lot of fun. JaMarcus Sheppard has taken the program over, and the QB/WR combo of Braden Atkinson and Jesse LeGree has been lighting it up every week. But this week they're facing a San Diego State defense that's better than its numbers suggest. The Aztecs' offense is bad (which helps with our play) and has put it in pretty tough positions. Even so, the Aztecs have done a decent job of limiting explosive plays, and that should help them here. They've also been respectable in the red zone. In fact, both these defenses have. Oregon State is allowing 3.75 points per red zone possession (28th nationally), and San Diego State is at 3.86 (34th). I can see Oregon State having to settle for more field goal attempts than it has so far, which makes the spread far less desirable, but makes the under pretty intriguing. The Pick: Under 53.5 (-110) at FanduelUpset of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Arizona at West VirginiaArizona is off to a 4-1 start, but last week's 34-7 blowout win over Cincinnati came with a cost. The team's leading receiver, Tre Spivey, is out for the year with a broken foot. We also don't know the status of fellow receivers Gio Richardson and Chris Hunter, who have also been banged up. Losing Spivey is a big blow, and if either Richardson or Hunter is limited or a no-go, that's a problem for an offense heading on the road to face a West Virginia team capable of putting points on the board in a hurry.If the Mountaineers can turn this game into a tennis match, it will play to their advantage. Arizona's defense has been pretty good on a down-to-down basis, ranking 10th nationally with a 66.7% success rate, but it's also been prone to allowing big plays. Plus, it hasn't exactly faced an offense as deadly as this West Virginia unit can be. title: Would a Marvin Harrison Jr. trade unlock his potential? History offers hope, and a warning - CBS Sports
description: When the Cardinals drafted Marvin Harrison Jr. fourth overall in 2024, he was all but anointed a future Hall of Famer. And after what he
body:
When the Cardinals drafted Marvin Harrison Jr. fourth overall in 2024, he was all but anointed a future Hall of Famer. And after what he did at Ohio State, it didn't take much imagination to envision what his NFL career might look like. Thirty-three games later, we're having a very different conversation: Would Harrison be better off playing somewhere other than Arizona?Maybe.But trading for Harrison requires believing two things: that the Cardinals haven't gotten the most out of him, and that another team can do better. The first argument is getting easier to make. The second is where things get complicated, especially when you look at what's happened to other highly drafted receivers who fell short of expectations early in their careers.With the NFL trade deadline approaching, that's worth examining.The No. 4 pick comes with expectationsIn my recent story on Carnell Tate, the fourth pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, we looked at what teams should expect from receivers drafted in the top 10. The average rookie season over the last decade was 901 receiving yards. Harrison finished with 885 in 2024, a respectable start, even if it fell short of expectations.But things haven't gotten better. Harrison managed 608 yards in 12 games last season, and through four games in 2026, he has five catches for 85 yards. For perspective, Seahawks rookie running back Jadarian Price, who played three games before landing on IR, has four receptions. This is the same Price who was targeted just 14 times over his final two seasons at Notre Dame. Harrison was targeted at least 13 times in four different games during his final season at Ohio State.
So yeah.Through 33 NFL games, Harrison has 1,578 receiving yards. Amari Cooper, also drafted fourth overall, had 2,285 yards at the same point. Corey Davis, the fifth pick in 2017, had 1,503. Harrison's production looks much closer to Davis's than Cooper's.Harrison vs. first-round receivers early in their careersStatisticHarrison1st-round WR avg.Rank (53 WRs)Receiving yards/game47.853.033rdReceptions/game3.273.7335thReceiving TD/game0.390.3017thCatch rate53.5%59.3%46thYards/target7.818.2231stYards after catch/reception2.54.5T-51stExplosive catches/target20.8%18.4%9thThere are encouraging numbers here. Harrison's 13 touchdowns are more than Cooper (12) or CeeDee Lamb (11) had through their first 33 games. He's also ninth in explosive receptions per target. But he's near the bottom in catch rate and yards after the catch. The big plays are there; the consistent production isn't.Harrison is playing more, but producing lessPerhaps the biggest concern isn't simply that Harrison has struggled. It's that he's becoming less involved in Arizona's offense, even while playing more.Among 41 first-round receivers in their first four appearances of Year 3, Harrison ranks 39th in receiving yards and is tied for the fewest receptions.Harrison's disappearing opportunitiesStatisticFirst 29 games2026 (4 games)Typical Year 3 1st-round WRReceiving yards/game51.521.364.8Targets/game6.53.37.5Catch rate54.5%38.5%60.9%Routes/game31.835.532.3Targets per route20.5%9.2%22.7%That last row tells the story. Harrison was targeted on roughly one of every five routes through his first 29 games. This season, it's fewer than one in 10. And that raises a fair question: Is Harrison struggling because he isn't getting opportunities, or is he not getting opportunities because he's struggling?There's evidence for both. Harrison ran 17 go routes in the first two games, tied for sixth most in the league, and Jacoby Brissett took some responsibility after Harrison went without a catch. But we can't blame everything on the quarterback or scheme when Trey McBride and Michael Wilson have combined for 58 receptions through four games. Harrison has five.Getting better isn't the same as becoming a starDespite the social-media noise, I'd be careful about giving up on Harrison. Plenty of first-round receivers have needed time to develop, but there's a difference between becoming productive and becoming the player a team thought it was drafting.Corey Davis, Mike Williams and DeVante Parker all improved after modest beginnings. Each had at least one season that justified some of that early optimism. The problem? None consistently produced like the elite receiver his draft position suggested. And Davis was drafted the highest of the three, at No. 5 overall, one spot after Harrison.Then there's Lamb, who went from a good young player to one of the NFL's best. But he was already averaging more than 62 yards per game through 33 appearances, considerably better than Harrison's 47.8.How other first-round WRs developedWR (draft pick)First 33 games YPGGames 34+ YPGNotable later seasonMarvin Harrison Jr. (4th)47.8TBDTBDCorey Davis (5th)45.555.9984 yards (2020)DeVante Parker (14th)44.748.71,202 (2019)Mike Williams (7th)35.751.41,146 (2021)Marquise Brown (25th)48.143.61,008 (2021)CeeDee Lamb (17th)62.690.41,749 (2023)Amari Cooper (4th)69.266.01,250 (2023)Williams and Parker eventually had 1,000-yard seasons, and Davis nearly got there with 984 in 2020. Harrison is young enough to make a similar leap. But Cooper and Lamb were already much more productive at this stage. That's an important distinction.What a trade can (and can't) fixSo what happens when a first-round receiver gets a fresh start somewhere else?Amari Cooper is the obvious success story. In 2018, Oakland traded him to Dallas, where his production jumped from 46.7 to 80.6 yards per game. He followed that with consecutive 1,000-yard seasons. Brandin Cooks also flourished after New England acquired him from New Orleans in 2017, producing 1,082 yards before adding 1,204 with the Rams the following year.But here's the difference: Both Cooper and Cooks had already posted two 1,000-yard seasons before being traded. Their new teams weren't betting on production they'd never seen. They were building on what those receivers had already done.The other historical comparisons aren't nearly as encouraging.I looked at first-round receivers traded in Year 3 or Year 4, the same stage of Harrison's career. Some joined better offenses or played with better quarterbacks. Most never became the players their new teams hoped they would.First-round WR trades in Years 3-4: Price and productionReceiverTraded from → toTrade returnBefore tradeAfter tradePhillip Dorsett (2017)Colts → PatriotsJacoby Brissett528 yards (2016)194 (2017)290 (2018)397 (2019)Corey Coleman (2018)Browns → Bills7th305 (2017)Released by BUF71 with NYG (2018)Jalen Reagor (2022)Eagles → Vikings7th + conditional 4th/5th299 (2021)104 (2022)138 (2023)100 (2024)Jahan Dotson (2024)Commanders → Eagles3rd + two 7ths; 5th sent with Dotson518 (2023)216 (2024)262 (2025)Brandin Cooks (2017)Saints → Patriots1st + 3rd; 4th sent with Cooks1,173 (2016)1,082 (2017)1,204 (2018)583 (2019)Sammy Watkins (2017)Bills → RamsE.J. Gaines + 2nd; 6th sent with Watkins430 in 8 games (2016)593 (2017)519 (2018)673 (2019)Kelvin Benjamin (2017)Panthers → Bills3rd + 7th475 in 8 CAR games217 in 6 BUF games380 (2018)Amari Cooper (2018)Raiders → Cowboys1st280 in 6 OAK games725 in 9 DAL games1,189 (2019)1,114 (2020)N'Keal Harry (2022)Patriots → Bears7th184 (2021)116 (2022)no rec (2023)Hollywood Brown (2022)Ravens → Cardinals1st; 3rd sent with Brown1,008 (2021)709 (2022)574 (2023)91 in 2g (2024)Cooper is the clearest example of a receiver taking his game to another level. Cooks maintained his production, while Sammy Watkins remained useful without ever returning to his 1,000-yard form.But Dorsett, Coleman, Reagor, Dotson and Harry? None became the player their original teams envisioned. Injuries played a role in some cases, but changing teams didn't solve the larger problem. And that's something any team considering Harrison should remember.The price needs to reflect the gambleOf course, there's another reason Harrison could be appealing: his contract. An acquiring team would inherit his remaining 2026 salary and 2027 compensation, with the possibility to exercise his fifth-year option for 2028.But what should it cost to acquire him?The historical returns vary considerably. Dallas sent a first-rounder for Cooper. New England gave up a first and third for Cooks, getting a fourth back. Arizona surrendered a first for Hollywood Brown, with a third coming back. All three receivers had already proved themselves.Meanwhile, Dotson cost a third and two sevenths, with a fifth going the other way. Harry and Coleman each brought back seventh-round picks.Harrison falls somewhere in between. He won't fetch a first-rounder, and a third feels closer to his worth given his production and untapped potential. But remember, Pittsburgh got a 2028 second-round pick for Joey Porter Jr. when plenty of people thought a third was the best-case scenario.Put another way: You never know. If one team believes it can unlock Harrison, a second-rounder might feel like a bargain. But at that price, the buyer better have a plan for how to use him.Arizona doesn't have to trade him, either. The Cardinals could spend the rest of 2026 seeing whether Mike LaFleur can figure this out. If they do make Harrison available, though, here are three teams I think would be intriguing landing spots.Three teams that could make sense
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New England PatriotsYes, the Pats traded for A.J. Brown, and he's the unquestioned No. 1 when he returns. But we've seen this group struggle without him. Receivers can't get open, Drake Maye has looked frazzled, and while Romeo Doubs looked better against Buffalo, he's better suited as a No. 3. Harrison could slide in as the No. 2, getting plenty of looks with defenses focused on Brown, without the same pressure he's faced in Arizona.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kansas City ChiefsAlways bet on Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes. That's where the conversation starts. Injuries to Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton (who could be done for the season) have also raised questions about depth. Thornton, a former Patriots second-round pick, is a great example of a receiver who struggled with his original team before finding success catching passes from Mahomes. Maybe Harrison could follow a similar path.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Indianapolis ColtsThis makes sense for sentimental and real-world football reasons. Harrison's father spent his Hall of Fame career catching passes from Peyton Manning in Indianapolis, and his son could follow in his footsteps there.But there's also a need. Alec Pierce's injury has created an opportunity outside, with Josh Downs and Tyler Warren already playing well. Harrison would give Daniel Jones another option without having to carry the offense. When Pierce returns, what currently looks like a weakness could become a strength if Harrison starts putting it together.The gambleI think Harrison can be better than he's been in Arizona. We all saw what he did at Ohio State, and we've seen flashes of that ability in the NFL. The issue has been consistency.The tougher questions are how much better he can be, and what another team should give up to find out.Cooper showed that a change of scenery can work. But history also shows how often a fresh start changes very little, particularly for receivers who haven't already established themselves as consistently productive.

title: NFL trade deadline: 10 candidates who could be on the move and teams that could be buyers, sellers - CBS Sports
description: Now that we are in October, we are officially just one month away from a significant date on the NFL's calendar: the trade deadline.Once
body:
Now that we are in October, we are officially just one month away from a significant date on the NFL's calendar: the trade deadline.Once 4 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 10, passes, all NFL teams are prohibited from trading players away. Last year's trade deadline was rather dramatic, as the New York Jets shipped off a couple of star players in cornerback Sauce Gardner and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams. The Jacksonville Jaguars made a vital addition in wide receiver Jakobi Meyers, and the Seattle Seahawks added a key returner in Rashid Shaheed, who contributed to their Super Bowl run. This year, we've already seen the Baltimore Ravens acquire a new center in Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles, the Dallas Cowboys trade two draft picks for former Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr., and the New York Giants send a fifth-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings for J.J. McCarthy in the wake of the Jaxson Dart injury. Who could be next? Below, we will break down 10 players who could potentially be on the trade block, plus a handful of teams that could be buyers or sellers over the next month.

        
            
                Cam Jurgens trade grades: Eagles send two-time Pro Bowl center to the Ravens for two draft selections
                
                    Jordan Dajani                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Potential trade candidates1. WR Marvin Harrison Jr., Cardinals
Given how this season has started, it's fair to list former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr. as a potential trade target. The Arizona Cardinals wideout has never averaged more than 52 yards per game in any of his three seasons, and his production is trending the wrong way. Through four games, Harrison has caught just five passes for 85 yards and one touchdown. During Sunday's loss to the Giants, he played 65.2% of snaps on offense. He's looked slow running routes and has struggled with drops, too. Last year, Harrison had to fight through a myriad of injuries, including an appendectomy and a foot issue. One could speculate that some of his struggles have been mental, so a change of scenery would make sense. However, the Cardinals aren't just going to punt on their former No. 4 overall pick.The Athletic has reported that the Cardinals are not desperate to deal Harrison — at least not yet. That could change if a team is willing to offer considerable compensation, but what kind of compensation would Arizona want, and would any team actually meet that price? Harrison is under contract for 2027, but his team will have to decide on his fifth-year option this upcoming offseason. 
Potential landing spot: Indianapolis Colts2. EDGE Khalil Mack, Chargers
ESPN mentioned Los Angeles Chargers pass rusher Khalil Mack as a trade candidate this past week. This is a 35-year-old player on an expiring deal, playing for a team that's arguably the biggest disappointment in the NFL this season. He should be helping a team that's contending.Mack has actually recorded three sacks in four games for the lowly Chargers this season to go along with 14 tackles and 13 pressures. The former No. 5 overall pick was named Defensive Player of the Year in 2016 and is only three years removed from his last double-digit sack season, recording a career-high 17 QB takedowns in 2023. Wouldn't it be something if he returned to Chicago, where he spent 2018-2021? Potential landing spot: Chicago Bears3. EDGE Josh Sweat, Cardinals
Let's talk about another Cardinal. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that pass rusher Josh Sweat has been a trade target for some time now. It makes sense. He reunited with his former defensive coordinator, Jonathan Gannon, in 2025, signing a four-year, $76.4 million deal with the Cardinals prior to the 2025 season. He recorded a career-high 12 sacks for the 3-14 Cardinals, and then his coach was fired. 
The Super Bowl champion is in his age-29 season and has played 50% of defensive snaps this year. Maybe reuniting him with Gannon again in Green Bay is a possibility, but what about returning to the team that drafted him in the fourth round back in 2018? Potential landing spot: Philadelphia Eagles4. WR Brian Thomas Jr., Jaguars 
Brian Thomas Jr. hit the ground running in the NFL, catching 87 passes for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie in 2024. He was the fourth rookie since 1970 to cross 1,200 yards receiving and double-digit touchdowns, joining an elite list that includes Randy Moss, Odell Beckham Jr. and Ja'Marr Chase. However, his production has since fallen off, and his role has diminished. BTJ caught 48 passes for 707 yards and just two touchdowns in 2025, while dropping 10 passes — tied for second-most in the NFL. This season, Thomas has caught nine passes for 105 yards and one touchdown in four games. He's played under 63% of offensive snaps in each game this year, and is averaging just 26.3 yards per game. It felt like his play forced the Jaguars to go out and pick up Jakobi Meyers at last year's trade deadline, who came in and led the team in targets (61), receptions (42) and receiving yards (483) from the day he was acquired to the end of the regular season. 
If the Jags trust rookie Josh Cameron will continue to ascend, could Jacksonville entertain offers for Thomas?Potential landing spot: Las Vegas Raiders5. OL Walker Little, Jaguars
Walker Little has been mentioned as a trade candidate for several months now for a couple of different reasons. One, Little has been benched for Cole Van Lanen, but he has also played snaps at every position along the offensive line, minus center. He's made 39 starts in 74 games played, and should receive interest if he were available.The Jaguars wouldn't want to part ways with their swing tackle for no reason, so any interested team better have an offer worth considering. We've seen the Jaguars trade offensive tackles at the deadline before, as they shipped Cam Robinson to the Vikings in October 2024. Granted, Robinson was on an expiring deal. That is not true for Little. 
Potential landing spot: Green Bay Packers6. RB Tony Pollard/Tyjae Spears, Titans
The top two running backs for the Tennessee Titans are on expiring deals, and one could be moved if the right team comes calling. Tony Pollard is averaging 55.3 rushing yards per game this season with one touchdown, but he and Derrick Henry are actually the only players to have reached 1,000 yards rushing in each of the last four seasons. He recorded a career-high 1,082 rushing yards in 2025.As for Tyjae Spears, he's a playmaker who just hasn't had the impact the Titans thought he would when he was selected in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft. He reached 800 scrimmage yards as a rookie but hasn't crossed 550 yards in a single season since, and he missed nine games over the last two years due to injury. I thought the Packers could have traded for one of these players instead of Kaleb Johnson before the regular season. Could Green Bay double-dip in the RB trade market if it receives bad news regarding Josh Jacobs' situation?  Potential landing spot: Green Bay Packers or Philadelphia Eagles7. EDGE Josh Uche, Dolphins
The former Patriot spent last year with the Eagles and then signed a one-year deal with the Miami Dolphins. He's recorded 17 tackles and one sack with four QB hits over the first four games of the season, and really stood out on the defensive front during Sunday's loss to the Vikings. With Josh Uche being four years older than former first-round pick Chop Robinson, he may be the player that's easier to acquire for a contender looking for pass-rush help. PFF ranks Uche 27th among 108 qualified edge defenders this season. 
Potential landing spot: Baltimore Ravens8. EDGE Kayvon Thibodeaux, Giants
Kayvon Thibodeaux was expected to step up with Brian Burns' season-ending injury, but he recorded just two combined tackles and zero sacks playing 95.5% of defensive snaps vs. the Cardinals on Sunday. He's had just one quarterback hurry in four games played. The former No. 5 overall pick out of Oregon recorded 11.5 sacks in 2023 but has had just eight since. Thibodeaux has been the subject of trade rumors for quite some time now. It remains to be seen if the Giants would want to move him for a Day 3 pick, but why not if Joe Schoen/John Harbaugh have no interest in signing him to a new deal? A change of scenery could give him a boost. Potential landing spot: Cleveland Browns9. LB Cedric Gray, Titans
Here's an interesting one. In his first full season as a starter last year, Cedric Gray racked up 164 tackles. That ranked fourth in the NFL and was the most tackles recorded by a Titan in a single season. It looked like Tennessee found a legitimate starter at linebacker, but after he missed the season opener due to a concussion, Gray has played less than 50% of defensive snaps in each of the last three games. He played 90.7% of defensive snaps in 2025. It would appear rookie Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton are Robert Saleh's top linebackers, making Gray available should there be an interested team.
Potential landing spot: Denver Broncos10. CB Kelee Ringo, Eagles
Kelee Ringo needs a change of scenery and is in the final year of his rookie deal. The former fourth-round pick out of Georgia has the physical makeup you want at 6-foot-2, 207 pounds. He's started in just eight of 55 career games played with the Eagles, and he has played only on special teams this season. However, there are multiple teams out there that need cornerbacks right now to come in and contribute immediately. Potential landing spot: Carolina Panthers or Detroit Lions Buyers and sellers
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buyer: Detroit LionsThe Lions have to do something about their defense, and firing Kelvin Sheppard probably isn't the answer. This unit has allowed 31.8 points per game, which ranks worst in the NFL, and allowed Bryce Young to look like prime Peyton Manning on Sunday night. I mean, Carolina shouldn't be dropping 445 total yards and 32 points on a team that expects to be a contender. The Lions also struggled to beat the Jets at home, and of course, were eviscerated by Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills in Week 2. One or two additions won't completely save this Lions defense, but they need to try. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seller: Tampa Bay BuccaneersThis season has been a disaster for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. They just registered their first 0-4 start since 2013, and quarterback Baker Mayfield is expected to miss a couple more weeks after dislocating the thumb on his throwing hand. Looking at the Bucs' schedule, you have to wonder when that first win of the season is coming. If a 0-4 start turns into a 0-7 start, Tampa Bay could be selling off some pieces. 
Could the Vita Vea market spark up again? What about veteran wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr.? Pass rusher YaYa Diaby is on an expiring deal, as is offensive guard Cody Mauch. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buyer: Indianapolis ColtsTeam owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put head coach Shane Steichen and general manager Chris Ballard on notice this season. While they most recently defeated the Washington Commanders in London, the offense recorded just 257 total yards and lost the turnover battle 2-1. The Colts defense ranks second-worst in total yards allowed per game, while the offense ranks eighth-worst and has to find a way to create explosive plays without Alec Pierce. With all that being said, the Colts still look like the second-best team in the division, so they could be shopping at the trade deadline. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seller: Los Angeles ChargersWe talked about the Chargers being arguably the biggest disappointment in the NFL this season, and if things continue to spiral, Joe Hortiz could look to sell some pieces. The 35-year-old Khalil Mack looks like an obvious target for contenders, but L.A. has another interesting pass rusher in Tuli Tuipulotu.
Tuipulotu made the Pro Bowl last year after recording 13 sacks, and just had a great outing in Seattle on Sunday, recording six tackles, half a sack, his first career interception and one forced fumble. He's in the final year of his rookie deal, and if the Chargers aren't going to pay him, they're better off trading him. Other potential trade targets could be wide receiver Quentin Johnston or veteran cornerback Donte Jackson.
        
            
                Chargers fire sale at NFL trade deadline? Landing spots for Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu
                
                    Jordan Dajani                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buyer: Cleveland BrownsCould the Browns actually be BUYERS at the trade deadline?! They exit Week 4 atop the AFC North with a 3-1 record. Deshaun Watson is playing the best football of his Cleveland career, and this defense is feisty even without Myles Garrett. I think Andrew Berry could be in the market for a defensive lineman or a pass rusher as he looks to build on this newfound momentum. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seller: Miami DolphinsThe Dolphins knew this season was going to be a grind, as general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and Jeff Hafley continue to get situated and try to navigate this rebuild. Miami has started 0-4 for the first time since 2019 and is the fifth team in the past 40 seasons to not lead in a game through Week 4.The Dolphins don't exactly have a plethora of tradeable assets like the Jets did last year, but a team could come calling for pass rushers Josh Uche and Chop Robinson, or maybe defensive lineman Zach Sieler.

The Braves were eliminated by the Dodgers on Wednesday, and Acuña finished the postseason with a .125 batting average

        The Atlanta Braves were eliminated in the NLDS at home on Wednesday, and, in the late innings, the Truist Park crowd let Ronald Acuña Jr. hear about it. Acuña was booed after grounding out in the seventh inning, after the Braves had just fallen behind in the game 3-1. The Los Angeles Dodgers went on to win the game 4-1 and the series 3-1.  "That's the first time that they boo me here at home, but I can't control that," Acuña said after Game 3 (via MLB.com). "... It's hard because I didn't do anything (to help) my team or my teammates. It's the hardest time."      Acuña played through a knee issue that limited him to DH in Game 3, coming out of an off day. He had a poor postseason, going 3 for 24 (.125) without an extra-base hit. Acuña has hit .189/.328/.226 in 15 postseason games since 2022. The fan base's frustration with Acuña and the Braves reached a boiling point Wednesday, hence the boos.  Of course, Acuña is hardly the only Braves player to fall flat in October. Matt Olson is a .206/.292/.349 postseason hitter with Atlanta. Drake Baldwin went 3 for 27 (.111) this postseason. Austin Riley is a career .213/.275/.354 postseason hitter. Pretty much every Braves hitter other than Ozzie Albies and Michael Harris II deserved boos this October. The numbers:
PAAVG/OBP/SLGHRRBIAlbies and Harris 				 				60 				 				.333/.424/.667 				 				3 				 				9 				 				Everyone Else 				 				198 				 				.137/.255/.208 				 				3 				 				11 				 				Atlanta's offense started this season extremely well. They averaged 5.27 runs per game through May, one of the highest marks in the game, then they slumped down to 4.08 runs per game after June 1. That is well below the 4.48 runs per game league average. It was a bad postseason for the offense, for sure, but the Braves bats had underwhelmed for months leading up to it.  Acuña, 29 in December, authored .255/.345/.451 batting line with 20 home runs and 21 stolen bases in 107 games around injuries this season. The 2023 NL MVP has been limited to 251 of 486 possible regular-season games the last three years due to injuries, most notably a torn ACL in 2024.  The Braves hold $17 million club options on Acuña for 2027 and 2028, and no matter how much the fans boo, those are absolute no-brainers. Of course the Braves will pick those up. Acuña remains one of the best bargains in baseball.  
Atlanta went 94-68 and won the NL East this year. This year's Wild Card Series win over the Philadelphia Phillies was their first postseason series win since their 2021 World Series title.

title: George Pickens stats: How Cowboys WR is helping fuel CeeDee Lamb's historic season - CBS Sports
description: Pickens may not be leading the box score, but his ability to draw coverage and create explosive plays has become
body:
Pickens may not be leading the box score, but his ability to draw coverage and create explosive plays has become a key ingredient in Dallas' offensive success
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:24 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys' (2-2) offense is once again humming through the first quarter of the 2026 season. Their Dak Prescott-led attack 30.5 points per game, and the most points per drive (3.39) in the league. Naturally, Prescott's numbers are elite: he ranks fifth in the league in EPA per dropback (0.24), fourth in completion percentage (70%), seventh in passing yards (1,065), tied for seventh in passing touchdowns (eight) and tied for seventh in passer rating (105.0). CeeDee Lamb has been on the receiving end of much of that production, leading the league in catches (37), receiving yards (498) and receiving first downs (28). Those 498 yards receiving are the most through the first four games of a season in Cowboys history. But what about George Pickens?Pickens has been a statistical casualty of Dallas' defensive struggles leading to the Cowboys having a league-low 36 drives this season. In 2026, playing alongside a healthy Lamb, Pickens has 225 yards receiving and no touchdowns on 18 catches through four weeks while averaging a career-low 12.5 yards per reception at the moment. However, Pickens is as valuable as ever if you ask the Cowboys.
"I think if you look at George last year, I don't know, you guys can look it up. I don't think he was putting up the insane numbers even till week four, five, six, whatever it was, because I think it's when CeeDee kind of went out, but George is learning the system as well. George easily could have had three catches for 180 yards in that game [on Sunday in the 34-30 win at the Houston Texans]," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "He really could have. He caught one with his eyes covered, and he opens people up all the time."  Pickens' role in the 2026 Cowboys offense, often, is that of the sacrificial lamb (pun intended) or field stretcher to open things up in the intermediate areas of the field. Pickens has run 45 go routes this season, the second-highest frequency in the league behind only DK Metcalf's 47 per TruMedia. Despite his high number of vertical routes deep down the field, Prescott maintains they're not making Pickens play decoy over and over again, even though that's what it may look like to the naked eye. "He's pulling two guys with him almost all the time, and I don't know if he's clearing guys out," Prescott said. "Those are all real routes, and if you want to leave one guy on them, I'm going to throw it to him. So that's just making the defense show us what they want to do. When we're sending them deep, as I said, if it's going to be one-on-one, I'm going to throw it down there [to Pickens]. If not, you've got to take another guy with him. and that gives us numbers advantage."
Prescott was true to his word on Sunday when Pickens finished with 75 yards receiving on two catches. His first catch of the day came deep down the left middle portion of the field for a 53-yard gain with 10:43 in the third quarter. The big play moved Dallas' offense from their own 36 to the Texans' 11. Nine plays later, Javonte Williams was in the end zone for one of his three rushing touchdowns that cut the Houston lead down to three, 23-20. 
When Dallas acquired Pickens in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers, many viewed him as temperamental after he appeared exasperated about not getting the football as the Steelers rotated through a revolving door of passers. His attitude has been anything but temperamental in Dallas. Some of that has to do with the knowledge that the Cowboys are trying to get him the football. Schottenheimer admitted he had a double move called for Pickens in which he was the No. 1 option on a play, but Prescott was hit in the pocket and couldn't get the throw downfield to him at that moment. What did Pickens do? He laughed it off. Only receiving three targets to Lamb's 21 on Sunday also didn't bother him because that happened to be Dallas' path to victory. "It'd be different if we weren't giving him the opportunities or trying to, and if defenses weren't just respecting him and taking him away," Prescott said. "So he's a guy that's smart, understands the game of football and he knows when the defenses are playing him that way, the opportunity it gives other guys. So he's a hell of a teammate, and I've said that. ... That [Pickens' attitude] shows a guy that's celebrating everybody else's success who obviously wants success, but as long as the team wins and he's doing his job, he's happy. We can't be more thankful for guys like that and with guys with an attitude like that."  
So, when will it be Pickens' turn? It could come as soon as tonight under the primetime lights at AT&T Stadium when the Cowboys host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-4) on "Thursday Night Football.""What I'm going to say about George is, if you blink, you're going [have] put up 150 [on you]," Schottenheimer said. "There's no doubt about that one, but the greatest thing about George Pickens was no one was happier in that locker room after the win than George Pickens, no one. It tells you how much of a magnetic personality he has, how much he loves playing football."

Georgia heads to Alabama in a massive SEC showdown, Nebraska hosts reigning champion Indiana, and the Red River Rivalry adds high drama to a pivotal week for the College Football Playoff race

        Week 6 of the college football has some major matchups on deck as two battles of undefeated programs headline the slate. Georgia and Alabama prepare to battle in Tuscaloosa in one of the marquee matchups of 2026, while Nebraska puts its undefeated mark on the line against the reigning national champs. As we get into conference play, though, the scope of the games shifts. Now, conference championship races are starting to take center stage, especially as disparate schedules stand out. The SEC race especially looks closer than ever with tiebreakers dotting the horizon, and the Pac-12 could experience a major upheaval if Fresno State can upset its standard-bearer. Here are six major matchups that will have major implications on the College Football Playoff race. No. 2 Georgia at No. 6 AlabamaThe battle in Tuscaloosa ranks among the best matchups of the season, and the winner will have a serious shot at No. 1 in the country. The Bulldogs are totally unimpeachable and have dominated teams on both sides of the ball amidst a spotless start. 
But through five games, Alabama looks back to business. The Crimson Tide are averaging a nation-leading 50 points against Power Four competition, including a 56-23 shellacking of Mississippi State last week. Keelon Russell looks like one of the best SEC quarterbacks in years; will it be enough? No. 7 Indiana at NebraskaThe second battle of undefeateds takes place in Lincoln as the unranked Cornhuskers host the reigning national champions. Nebraska hasn't played a quality opponent, but they're beating teams by an average of 29.4 points per game. Indiana is the first major prove-it spot. The Hoosiers are undefeated, but showed some flaws during a 29-23 win over Northwestern two weeks ago. With a win, Nebraska can firmly join the shortlist of Big Ten playoff contenders. With USC and Penn State sidelined, there's plenty of space. 
No. 22 Houston at Kansas StateA pair of one-loss teams battle to stay alive in the conference championship race. The Cougars needed a comeback to outlast UCF last week after a slow offensive start. Kansas State's loss to Cincinnati in the Big 12 opener was a stunner, but they've otherwise looked the part. The top-three group of Texas Tech, Utah and BYU are set in the Big 12, but the winner of this group could crash the party. No. 1 Texas vs. OklahomaMaybe this game doesn't belong on the list. The Sooners look the part of a total disaster after a 2-2 start, including one of the worst offenses in the nation. But it is the Red River Rivalry, and that means technically anything can happen. The Longhorns have been inconsistent since their furious comeback against Ohio State, including a 20-17 clunker against Tennessee. A dominant win could cement their spot at No. 1, even as Alabama and Georgia battle. A loss would be brutal as the Longhorns head into a stretch of five straight games against AP Top 20 opponents. 
No. 13 Oregon vs. No. 21 UCLATwo of the most exciting teams in the country meet in Eugene on Saturday. The Bruins are undefeated and look completely transformed under first-year coach Bob Chesney. While cross-city rival USC has struggled on cross-country road trips, UCLA obliterated Maryland 54-3 in their last game. Oregon is a different kind of challenge. The Ducks shook off an early loss to Oklahoma State to beat USC at The Coliseum, even with starting quarterback Dante Moore sidelined by a concussion. Backup Dylan Raiola will likely get the start against UCLA, and staying on track is vital with No. 5 Ohio State still left on the schedule. No. 10 LSU at KentuckyThe Tigers haven't had much chance to impress since losing to Ole Miss in Week 3, but a road trip to Kentucky is a potential get-right spot. The Wildcats sit at 4-1 after a stunning win over South Carolina, which caused Texas A&M to slip up at home. If LSU is a serious SEC contender, they'll show it against Kentucky. 
No. 23 Boise State at Fresno StateAt this point, the Pac-12 remains the overwhelming favorite to produce the Group of Six's berth in the CFP. No. 23 Boise State faces its biggest conference battle yet against Fresno State, perhaps the most underrated team in the conference. Since a poor showing against USC in the opener, the Bulldogs have been dominant, winning every game by at least 14 points. The line is only 6.5; don't be surprised if Fresno State pulls off a major upset.
